item.title: 217-day underwater patrol of UK's nuclear submarine HMS Vengeance worries experts
item.description: The Royal Navy's HMS Vengeance nuclear submarine has set a new record by completing a 217-day mission. For about seven months, the crew had almost no contact with the outside world.

item.title: Can Andy Burnham bring British brio back to Brussels?
item.description: Good morning. Leo Cendrowicz here, bringing you the Friday newsletter. And on today’s menu: UK PM Andy Burnham is in Brussels for an EU-UK summit, while we digest the Coalition of the Willing meeting and the Xi-Trump-Putin summit.

item.title: White House national cyber director fired after wave of tech outages
item.description: The national cyber director is tasked with advising the president on cybersecurity policy and strategy, including information security and data protection as well as deterrence of "malicious" activity.

item.title: Europe Today: Nigel Farage on Europe Today ahead of EU-UK summit
item.description: The European Union and the United Kingdom are holding a crucial summit in Brussels today to patch up ties after the bitter Brexit divorce. We speak with Reform UK leader Nigel Farage. We also debrief Trump, Putin and Xi's meeting in China with Ben Hodges, former General Commander of the US.

item.title: What are '2226' buildings and why don't they require heating or AC?
item.description: Euronews interviewed Astrid Lampl, architect and project director at the Baumschlager Eberle, which built the first heating and AC-free building in France, about the '2226' building method behind this achievement.

item.title: City or countryside: Where is the house price gap widest in Europe, and why?
item.description: Across Europe, homes in cities cost far more than in the countryside. However, smaller gaps do not mean that homes are affordable. Euronews Business looks at where the gap is widest and why.

item.title: Parents' mobile phone use outside work hours linked to delayed child speech development
item.description: Study finds that parents' use of mobile phones outside working hours is linked to poorer speech development in preschool children; researchers also warn that overly dependent family relationships can undermine youngsters' autonomy.

item.title: Are we making progress on climate action? 23 encouraging signs from COP31
item.description: New alliances, commitments and funding could help protect Pacific island nations, restore degraded peatlands and tackle global food waste.

item.title: New hotels in Europe in 2027 – the most anticipated openings and reopenings
item.description: Guests will be welcomed at a host of new European openings in 2027, including luxury city properties, wellness retreats and a hotel located in a former convent and prison.

item.title: Hungary to drop veto on Ukraine’s remaining EU accession clusters
item.description: Hungary is set to lift its objections to Ukraine’s last two EU accession clusters on Friday, diplomats say, allowing Kyiv and Moldova to start negotiating on every aspect of EU membership.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 20th, 2026 – Morning
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 20th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Stocks, gold and silver fall after blockbuster Anthropic IPO
item.description: Anthropic shares rose 17% on their Nasdaq debut, but the record IPO failed to halt a Wall Street sell-off. Asian stocks followed US markets lower on Friday, while gold and silver fell as investors braced for a US rate rise.

item.title: Exhibition uses AI to recreate people’s memories and raise awareness of dementia
item.description: AI-powered tools are offering new ways to help people with Alzheimer’s reconnect with personal memories.

item.title: US sells first deep-sea mining leases off American Samoa, days after court ruled against process
item.description: The Trump administration pressed ahead with the auction despite a federal judge’s finding that regulators broke wildlife protection law and conservation groups vowed to have the leases voided.

item.title: Ukraine: Russian strikes damage Austrian and Dutch embassies in Kyiv
item.description: Russian strikes damaged the Austrian and Dutch embassies in Kyiv on Thursday. Windows were shattered and vehicles damaged, but diplomatic staff escaped unharmed.

item.title: 10,000 identical inflatable rings raise questions over Ceuta migrant crossing
item.description: The report estimates that between 8,000 and 10,000 identical inflatable rings were used during the mass migrant crossing in July, suggesting they may have been purchased and distributed in advance.

item.title: Former UN General Assembly President joins Europe Tonight to debrief the latest COP31 talks
item.description: Euronews’ Evening Show Europe Tonight was joined by María Fernanda Espinosa, UN Secretary-General candidate and former UN General Assembly President, to debrief COP31 talks.

item.title: Nobel economist Joseph Stiglitz deems youth protests across Europe 'legitimate'
item.description: Nobel Prize-winning economist Joseph Stiglitz says young people are right to be worried and that youth protests across Europe are "legitimate".

item.title: Four men found guilty of raping woman drugged by husband in UK
item.description: Police uncovered hundreds of intimate images of Joanne Young after investigating her husband in 2024 for uploading images depicting bestiality, exposing a wider pattern of sexual abuse.

item.title: Europe Tonight discusses; Will Sánchez's bid to unite the left work?
item.description: Watch on Europe Tonight as Antonio Roldán, former member of parliament and professor at IE School of Politics, Economics and Global Affairs, discusses the upcoming elections with our presenter Mared Gwyn Jones.

item.title: Europe Tonight: Theresa Fallon on whether world leaders could redraw global spheres of influence
item.description: Euronews' Europe Tonight welcomes Theresa Fallon, founder and director of the Centre for Russia Europe Asia Studies, to discuss the APEC summit with presenter Mared Gwyn-Jones, including comparisons with the Yalta Conference and the possibility of leaders redrawing global spheres of influence.

item.title: COP 31: Is the rich world doing enough to support climate-vulnerable countries?
item.description: Euronews' weekly evening show Europe Tonight welcomes Sandrine Dixson-Declève, Honorary President of the Club of Rome, to discuss whether COP31 can be called a success, as well as whether the rich world is handing out crumbs to poorer countries grappling with the impacts of climate change.

item.title: Turkish court blocks jailed Istanbul mayor from 2028 presidential race
item.description: Imamoglu's office has released a copy of his business management degree from Istanbul University, awarded in 1995.

item.title: Europe Tonight : NATO Secretary General’s Head of Policy Planning debriefs the latest APEC talks
item.description: Euronews' evening show Europe Tonight welcomed Fabrice Pothier, head of policy planning in the private office of the Secretary General of NATO, he also oversees the review of current and future strategic policy issues facing NATO.

item.title: US defence secretary Pete Hegseth lands in Ecuador on Latin America anti-narcotics tour
item.description: The US defence secretary, under fire for his role in the Iran war and illegal bombings in the Caribbean and Pacific, has announced a military pact with Venezuela. His next stop is Honduras.

item.title: At least one dead and dozens missing after migrant boat capsizes off Senegal en route to Spain
item.description: The latest sinking comes amid a sharp rise in departures towards the Canary Islands, with more than 11,000 people reaching the Spanish archipelago in the first two weeks of November.

item.title: France to monitor YouTubers for political bias ahead of 2027 election
item.description: France will hold its presidential election on 18 April and 2 May next year, with far-right leader Marine Le Pen currently leading in opinion polls. Parliamentary elections are expected to follow in June.

item.title: Macron backs reopening 'the question' of Ukraine's NATO accession
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron said that Ukraine's NATO accession was brushed aside in early 2022 in a "completely different" context.

item.title: New regional security architecture will also benefit Europe, Pakistani FM tells Euronews
item.description: In an exclusive interview for Euronews’ World Conversation show, Pakistan’s Deputy Prime Minister revealed the backstage mediation that brought the US and Iran to agreement in June. He also outlined Pakistan's strategy towards a new regional security architecture in coordination with Europe.

item.title: European leaders reject 'Yalta 2.0' for Ukraine after Trump meets Putin and Xi
item.description: "A Yalta format will not bring peace," German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said at the end of a Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin just hours after Trump, Putin and Xi held talks in China.

item.title: Trump leaves China without meeting Kim Jong-un as trilateral summit raises concerns across Asia
item.description: The US, Chinese and Russian leaders pledged to hold talks on nuclear risk reduction, but made no mention of North Korea in their joint peace declaration.

item.title: Euronews Verify: Is Hungary turning the page on its rule of law problems?
item.description: Hungary is under new leadership, and reforms are underway. But can Péter Magyar restore the rule of law and win back the EU's trust?

item.title: US: Protesters warn of AI bubble as Anthropic makes stock market history
item.description: Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut with a record-breaking IPO valuing the AI company at $1.5 trillion. Outside the exchange in New York, police detained three protesters warning of financial risks.

item.title: On board with Frontex: Euronews patrols the waters off Crete as migrant arrivals from Libya rise
item.description: Aboard the Latvian patrol vessel Valpas, Euronews follows maritime operations and visits a Frontex drone base at Tympaki airfield. A search for missing migrants near Chrissi Island highlights the dangers of the crossing, while temporary reception facilities face growing pressure.

item.title: Trump questions Europe's billions in Ukraine aid during surprise call
item.description: The US president reportedly called into a meeting of Kyiv's European allies from Air Force One, hours after talks with Putin and Xi, and said Moscow was ready to negotiate a peace deal.

item.title: Middle East conflict poses biggest threat to global energy security in history, IEA warns
item.description: Disruption to oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz is driving up costs for households, while the agency says the longer the crisis continues, the harder it will be for global energy markets to recover.

item.title: Anthropic shares open 34% above IPO price in Nasdaq debut after record listing
item.description: Anthropic shares opened at $111.50 in their Nasdaq debut on Thursday, 34% above their $83 IPO price, putting the Claude maker on track for a $2 trillion valuation (€1.8tn) after it raised $81.3 billion (€74bn) in the largest initial public offering in history.

item.title: Europe Tonight: Trump, Putin and Xi hold talks as Ukraine allies meet in Berlin
item.description: Trump, Putin and Xi sign a joint declaration in China with no breakthrough on Ukraine, European leaders meet US envoys in Berlin, Spain’s election rivals debate, and COP31 talks enter their final stretch in Turkey.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 19th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 19th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Iraq orders armed factions to withdraw from strategic area amid alleged oil smuggling and US pressure
item.description: Prime Minister Ali Faleh al-Zaidi has given the Iran-backed group until Friday to leave Jurf al-Nasr, as Baghdad faces growing pressure from Washington to bring powerful militias under state control.

item.title: From Carthage to Grenoble: 'Les Carthagi'Noix' opens a window on Arab culture in France
item.description: In a city renowned for its walnut trees, and at a cultural distance that surpasses geography, a group of culture and art lovers chose to begin a new story called the dialogue between the Arab world and France.

item.title: EU health chief pelted with 'ashes' by pesticide protesters
item.description: Two protesters threw what appeared to be ashes at EU Health Commissioner during a cancer summit in Brussels, prompting a strong condemnation from von der Leyen.

item.title: MWC26 Doha ushers the IQ era defined by connectivity and inclusion
item.description: FOCUS heads to GSMA’s MWC26 in Doha, where AI readiness, cloud computing and the road to 6G networks take centre stage. Running alongside the ITU’s Plenipotentiary Conference for the first time, the event brings together 194 member states to advance global connectivity and digital transformation.

item.title: Beaujolais nouveau 2026: a fresh, light vintage hopes to revive a struggling sector
item.description: The party to celebrate the 2026 vintage of Beaujolais nouveau, said this year to be fruity, light and easy to drink: the ideal recipe for forgetting the sector’s crisis.

item.title: Islam to become world's largest religion by 2035 as Christianity also grows, study says
item.description: Pew Research Center has projected that both Islam and Christianity will grow between 2020 and 2070, with Muslims rising by more than 80% to over 3.6 billion and Christians by 30% to close to 3 billion.

item.title: AI being run in a 'medieval' way, says UN rights chief
item.description: UN high commissioner for human rights Volker Türk warned that while AI might sound something futuristic, underneath it is based on an age-old narrative of power.

item.title: EU moves towards 10-year probation period for new members - starting with Montenegro
item.description: EU ambassadors broadly backed a 10-year probation period for newcomers, with voting rights open to suspension for Orbán-style breaches, as a basis for Montenegro’s treaty.

item.title: EU must move beyond piecemeal trade deals with China, MEPs warn
item.description: MEPs are calling on the European Commission to “ease” the regulatory burden on EU companies and deploy “horizontal” trade defence tools to tackle Chinese competition.

item.title: Damaged buildings and debris after Ukrainian attack on Russia's Kursk
item.description: At least 11 people were injured after a Ukrainian attack damaged residential buildings and public facilities in the southwestern Russian city of Kursk, according to regional Governor Alexander Khinshtein.

item.title: Weakened Putin is pinning his hopes on a Le Pen victory, Browder says
item.description: Kremlin critic Bill Browder tells Euronews that a weakened Vladimir Putin is using peace talks to buy time, hoping a far-right victory in France will fracture European support for Ukraine.
